claim: Nagarajan et al. run a controlled ablation where all settings are held identical except whether nondeterministic GPU operations are enabled, and find the resulting variance in DQN training curves grows to look similar in magnitude to the variance from exploration randomness and weight-initialization randomness, sources they separately studied.
stance_target: N8: does prior work show a non-method execution-environment factor (GPU/platform-adjacent) moving results by an order comparable to other studied variance sources?
scope_conditions: Deep Q-learning (DQN), Atari-style benchmark, 10 million training timesteps, 5 runs per group
quoted_support: While the variance in game score is low for the first two million frames, it quickly increases and the variance in the learning curve looks similar to the curves for exploration and weight initialization.

claim: Nagarajan et al. state that GPU nondeterminism is uniquely important because it is the only studied source of nondeterminism that exists outside the algorithm itself, meaning even a fully reproduced implementation can still fail to reproduce results due to execution-environment (platform/library) effects.
stance_target: N8: is execution-environment (platform/library) variance documented as capable of moving results independent of method/implementation correctness?
quoted_support: The GPU is of special interest since it is the only source of nondeterminism that exists outside of the algorithm itself... Even if implementation details are successfully reproduced, sources of nondeterminism outside of the algorithm can considerably impact results.

claim: Nagarajan et al. do not report a single numeric percentage or effect-size ratio comparing GPU-nondeterminism-driven variance to method-difference variance; the comparison is qualitative/visual (comparable-looking curves), not a quantified ratio.
stance_target: N8: precision of the 'same order' quantification available in prior work
scope_conditions: Full-text grep, no percentage figures found for cross-source comparison
quoted_support: We use the standard deviations of the evaluations as a qualitative measure of the impact of a source of nondeterminism on achieving reproducibility.

claim: A widely-circulated web-search AI summary attributed figures of 74-87% of standard deviation being GPU-nondeterminism-driven to this line of research, but these exact figures do not appear anywhere in Nagarajan et al.'s extracted full text and should not be cited as sourced from this paper.
stance_target: Anti-fabrication check: verifying a search-engine-generated statistic against primary text
scope_conditions: Grep verification against 5,315-word extracted PDF text
